sections.title: Racks, Cabling & Documentation
sections.content:
Equipment mounts in 19-inch racks measured in U (1U = 1.75 in). Plan airflow: use a hot aisle / cold aisle layout so intakes face cold aisles and exhausts face hot aisles.
Structured cabling: horizontal runs from the IDF to wall jacks, backbone/vertical runs between MDF and IDFs. Terminate on patch panels (110 blocks) and jumper with patch cables.
Document everything: label both ends of every cable, keep a rack diagram/elevation, port maps, and an up-to-date network diagram. Good labeling is the difference between a 5-minute fix and an hour of tracing.
Cable management (trays, hooks, Velcro) keeps airflow and serviceability; avoid tight zip-tie bends that damage cable.
exam_tips: Hot aisle/cold aisle arranges racks so cold intake air and hot exhaust air don't mix.
Label both ends of every cable and keep rack diagrams + port maps current.
MDF = main distribution frame; IDFs connect back to it (star of closets).

sections.title: Power & Environment
sections.content:
Power protection:
UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) — battery backup for ride-through during outages and clean shutdown; also conditions power.
PDU (Power Distribution Unit) — distributes (and often meters/switches) power to rack gear.
Generator — long-term backup power.
Plan redundant power supplies and dual feeds (A/B power) for critical gear.
Environment: control temperature and humidity (HVAC); too humid = corrosion, too dry = static (ESD). Monitor with sensors. Fire suppression uses clean agents (not water) in equipment rooms.
Grounding/bonding and surge protection guard against electrical damage.
exam_tips: UPS = short-term battery (ride-through + clean shutdown); generator = long-term power.
A PDU distributes rack power; dual power supplies + A/B feeds give redundancy.
Control humidity: too low causes static/ESD, too high causes condensation/corrosion.

sections.title: Installation Factors & Safety
sections.content:
Follow cable standards and limits: 100 m copper max, keep data cable away from power lines and fluorescent ballasts (EMI), respect bend radius, and use plenum-rated cable in air-handling spaces.
MDF/IDF placement: central, secure, climate-controlled, with physical access control.
Use the right cable for the job (shielded in noisy areas, fiber for distance/EMI immunity, outdoor/direct-burial where needed).
Safety: lift properly, don't overload circuits, maintain an MSDS/SDS for chemicals, and keep clear egress. Rack-mount heavy gear low for stability.
exam_tips: Keep copper data cable away from power lines and ballasts to avoid EMI; use STP or fiber in noisy areas.
Plenum-rated cable is required in air-handling (plenum) spaces.
Mount heavy equipment low in the rack for stability and plan the PoE power budget.

concept_cards.hook: The 1.75-inch vertical increment of a 19-inch equipment rack; gear height is rated in U (1U, 2U, …).
A data-center layout that faces equipment intakes toward cold aisles and exhausts toward hot aisles to cool efficiently.
Uninterruptible Power Supply — battery backup that rides through short outages, conditions power, and allows clean shutdown.
Power Distribution Unit — distributes (and often meters/switches) electrical power to devices in a rack.
Main Distribution Frame (building's primary wiring hub) and Intermediate Distribution Frames (floor closets that connect back to it).
A standardized cabling system of horizontal runs (to jacks), backbone runs (between frames), patch panels, and documentation.
Supplying critical gear from two independent power sources (and dual power supplies) so one feed can fail without downtime.
The minimum curve a cable can take without degrading signal or damaging conductors/fiber; tight bends cause errors.

practice_questions.q: Which data-center layout improves cooling efficiency?
practice_questions.explanation: Hot aisle/cold aisle keeps cold intake and hot exhaust air separated for efficient cooling.

practice_questions.q: Which device provides short-term battery backup and clean shutdown during a power outage?
practice_questions.explanation: A UPS provides battery ride-through and conditioning; a generator covers long outages.

practice_questions.q: Which component distributes and often meters power to equipment within a rack?
practice_questions.explanation: A Power Distribution Unit distributes (and may meter/switch) power to rack devices.

practice_questions.q: Why keep data cabling away from fluorescent light ballasts and power lines?
practice_questions.explanation: Ballasts and power lines emit EMI that corrupts data on nearby unshielded copper.
